name: takt
why: A text-based music programming language, obscure and old, where composing means writing code that becomes sound.

brief.what_it_is: Takt is a text-based language for describing note and chord sequences, and algorithmic composition rules, with C-like syntax. The SourceForge page says the package contains three parts: a REPL (read-eval-play loop) interpreter for Takt, a MIDI-file-to-Takt translator (the mid2takt executable), and an Emacs interface that enables note entry from a MIDI keyboard. You write Takt code in, and it plays back as sound. The page does not describe the exact input and output formats.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation. Its framing is 'Text-based Music Programming Tools', so the idea is composing music by writing code rather than in a graphical sequencer.
brief.how_it_works: The page does not explain the mechanism in detail. It says the REPL interprets Takt code and plays the result, and that mid2takt converts MIDI files into Takt source. The project is listed as C++ with Emacs-Lisp.
brief.install_notes: The homepage is a SourceForge download page with a Download button. It lists two executables, mid2takt and takt. No build steps, runtime requirements, accounts, or first-run configuration appear on the page. The Emacs interface needs Emacs and a MIDI keyboard.
brief.standout: It is an old, text-first music language in C-like syntax that pairs a REPL with a MIDI-to-text converter and a live MIDI keyboard entry mode through Emacs. It is closer to a programmable score than to a DAW or a tracker.
brief.status: quiet. The SourceForge page marks it 'Status: Alpha', shows 'Last Update: 2016-01-27', and says the project was registered 2014-07-14. It shows 28 downloads this week. Nothing newer than January 2016 appears on the page.
brief.caveats: The URL I fetched is a SourceForge project page, not a project website with docs, and it shows no command examples or tutorials. Takt is marked Alpha. The license is GPLv2. The 'Last Update' date may refer to a file upload rather than a code commit. The page's description has a typo ('compositon'). I did not follow any further links, so syntax, platform support, and build details are unverified.
quotes: Takt is a text-based language for describing note and chord sequences as well as algorithmic compositon rules with C-like syntax.
This software package contains a REPL (read-eval-play loop) interpreter for Takt, a MIDI-file-to-Takt translator, and an Emacs interface program which enables note entry from a MIDI keyboard.
